title: Disentangled Representation Learning for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
claim: A multi-task encoder-decoder with a VAE over operator parameters yields disentangled, interpretable latent factors, with losses attached at each stage.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, brace labels below, dashed loss lines
description: A wide left-to-right architecture diagram. At far left, three stacked heatmaps show input functions f_i^η(x). Arrows lead to three columns of colored dots, the task-specific parameter vectors θ_P^η. These feed an orange trapezoid encoder, then a small latent vector z, then a teal decoder. A cream callout above z shows three MNIST digits (3, 4, 9) labeled b^η(x), captioned 'Interpretable physics discovery'. The reconstructed parameter vectors θ̂_P pass into a green rounded box of 'Iterative Fourier layers' (F, R, F⁻¹, +σ, W blocks). The output is θ_Q, then three output heatmaps u_i^η(x). A gray 'Loss' box lists data, KL, supervision and reconstruction losses, linked by dashed colored lines to the stages where each is computed. Curly braces underneath label Multi-task learning, First decoder and Second decoder.
caption: \NLL{Overview of the DisentangO architecture. Each task correspond to a different (hidden) PDE parameter $\bb$. For illustration, the same input function $f^\eta_i$ is shown for multiple tasks to highlight that different parameter fields $b^{\eta}$ can produce different output functions $u_i^{\eta}$ under identical input $f$; in practice, $f$ may vary across tasks. The task-specific lifting parameters $\theta_P^{\eta}$ are encoded and reconstructed through a VAE, and the reconstructed parameters $\hat{\theta}_P^{\eta}$ are fed into the iterative Fourier layers to form the task-specific neural operator $G^{\eta}$. Loss components are overlaid to indicate where each term in the objective $L_{loss}$ is computed. } \vspace{-0.2in}
abstract: Neural operators (NOs) excel at learning mappings between function spaces, serving as efficient forward solution approximators for PDE-governed systems. However, as black-box solvers, they offer limited insight into the underlying physical mechanism, due to the lack of interpretable representations of the physical parameters that drive the system. To tackle this challenge, we propose a new paradigm for learning disentangled representations from NO parameters, thereby effectively solving an inverse problem. Specifically, we introduce DisentangO, a novel hyper-neural operator architecture designed to unveil and disentangle latent physical factors of variation embedded within the black-box neural operator parameters. At the core of DisentangO is a multi-task NO architecture that distills the varying parameters of the governing PDE through a task-wise adaptive layer, alongside a variational autoencoder that disentangles these variations into identifiable latent factors. By learning these disentangled representations, DisentangO not only enhances physical interpretability but also enables more robust generalization across diverse systems. Empirical evaluations across supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised learning contexts show that DisentangO effectively extracts meaningful and interpretable latent features, bridging the gap between predictive performance and physical understanding in neural operator frameworks.
